note: The DECLARED, BOUNDED set the diff-scoped mutation gate may report NOT_APPLICABLE for instead of UNKNOWN, because the cost of measuring it has been measured and is not the diff's. Owner ruling 2026-10-03: ONE module-level declaration. A bare `module.py` key declares the whole module and needs `cost.scope: module` with both module measurements; a `module.py::function` key needs `cost.scope: function`. Exactly one module key is permitted — a second is a policy change, not an entry. Read mutation_diff.parse_exclusions for the shapes it refuses, declared_module for what matches, and declared_exclusion_status for the only transition allowed (UNKNOWN or NOT_RUN -> NOT_APPLICABLE; never a survivor cleared, never a PASS). The gate consults this at SELECTION, before the clean run, so a declared module costs seconds instead of the 7693 s #3238 spent reaching the same answer.
retiredWhen: mutmut applies the glob at GENERATION as well as at RUN, so a one-function diff stops paying for the module's whole population. capture.py then becomes measurable function by function and this file goes to empty — the exclusion is dated debt, not a design.

capture.py.reason: THIS IS A MODULE-LEVEL FACT, not a claim about any one function: `mutmut run <glob>` applies the glob when it RUNS mutants and never when it GENERATES them, so every capture.py diff pays for the whole module's population whatever it touched. No function of capture.py is measurable inside the 7200 s gate budget on the runner, and no narrowing of a diff reaches that cost. Measured twice, by two independent mechanisms: by TIME, #3238 presented the ideal case — one 87-line function and one keyword argument — and still reached no mutant, with selection plus clean run 1337 s, generation under 1 s, then a silent traced stats pass of at least 7556 s; 618 spinner lines carried ZERO `N/M` ticks, which is what proves nothing was tested rather than merely slow. By MEMORY, one `mutmut run` worker reached 8.2 GB RSS importing the 536 MB generated module — above the fleet's 8 GB standing per-process limit, while mutmut spawns one worker per core — and was killed by hand after 21 minutes with `--timeout 900` never firing. Superseded E7's two function keys (`capture.py::_cpap_stream_watch_row`, `capture.py::_maybe_start_cpap_spool_pull`), which could never fire once this key exists; their measurements are the evidence cited here.
